'''Unobtainable items''' are [[items]] that exist within the game's code, but cannot ever be obtained by players via normal gameplay. These items are usually found by extracting information via the game's cache. Some of these items are found in game, but cannot be placed into the [[inventory]].

These items, like all other items, have an ID number assigned to them. [[Item IDs]] may change over certain updates, and may fill unused IDs that are considered null. Certain items used exclusively may be removed from the game and their item IDs relabeled as "Null", which are represented in the cache as [[pink skirt]]s.

==Never released==
These items have never appeared in the game in any form. Usually, they are items leftover from content that was significantly altered or removed during development, making them useless.

Items with no ID were deleted from the game before the release of the [[Update:RS2 Beta Item test|RS2 Beta Item test]] on 3 March 2004.

==Gnome Restaurant==
These items all previously could be obtained during the [[Gnome Restaurant]] minigame. Originally, players had to add each ingredient individually, which was a painstaking process and would produce Odd food if a mistake was made at any point. On [[7 August]] [[2006]] the minigame was reworked, with the majority of ingredients now being added at once via a new interface. As a result, these items have never been obtainable in ''Old School RuneScape''.

==Joke items==
Other items could never be made into banknotes to begin with, yet nevertheless an ID slot was taken up by a null item where the noted form would have been. In 2005, these empty slots were filled by items with humorous names and descriptions that all bizarrely had the appearance of a [[Pink skirt]]. Players who attempted to either spawn or view the items using memory editing software would be given a [[Hex edit detected]] instead. In ''RuneScape 3'', these items would later become viewable in the Quick Chat interface causing much confusion.

While originating as filler items for redundant ID slots, some were repurposed to serve new ends: as metadata could still be assigned to the item, the pink skirts could be read by others scripts as a sort of look-up table.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1634704669271285760|date=11 March 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/106746|archivedate=12 March 2023|quote=Metadata can be written on them, then read by other scripts as a sort of look-up table. Doesn't involve anyone actually receiving the item. It may sound odd, but when RuneScript had fewer features in the language, this was a remarkably effective way of storing game metadata.}}
